headline: Democrats sweep midterms, gain Senate majority, vow to rein in Trump
summary: The Democratic Party secured control of both the Senate and House of Representatives, setting the stage for a period of political deadlock and intense scrutiny of President Donald Trump's administration.
details: Democrats have vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington. This marks the first time Trump will contend with an opposition-controlled Congress.

Despite the significant defeat for his party, Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom, telling reporters it was "relaxing" for him. He briefly acknowledged the election results, noting his veto power.

A wave of anger over Trump's policies, particularly the US-Iran war's role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, flipping seats in deeply Republican states for a majority of at least 54-44. Democrats also gained at least 30 seats in the House of Representatives.

House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries stated that the incoming majority would focus on affordability and accountability, asserting that the House would no longer function as a "wholly owned subsidiary of the Trump administration."

Voters in conservative strongholds, who propelled Trump to his second term just two years prior, swung dramatically towards Democrats. This shift was fueled by deep frustration over the unpopular war with Iran, anxiety over the high cost of living, and anger at Trump's stewardship.
Notable victories include Democrats ending a decades-long losing streak in Texas, winning their first Senate seat there since 1988, and electing Kansas's first Democratic senator in nearly a century.

Once seated in January, Democrats are expected to use their power to investigate Trump's administration, family, and allies, and demand concessions on major legislation. The Democratic Senate can also block Trump's nominees, including any US Supreme Court justices.
The Democratic victory is also fueling questions about the longevity of the Supreme Court's two eldest justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, and the durability of its conservative majority.
Trump acknowledged the war with Iran had played a role in his party's losses but stood by his decision. Vice President JD Vance also attributed the losses to the decision to attack Iran in February.

headline_marked: [[Two DGFI members dismissed, jailed]] for one year over Mohammadpur extortion attempt
headline: Two DGFI members dismissed, jailed for one year over Mohammadpur extortion attempt
summary: Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were found guilty in a court martial for confining and assaulting a businessman in Dhaka, demanding Tk 10 lakh.
details: Two Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) members, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each. This follows a court martial where they were found guilty of an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a businessman in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.

The incident occurred on October 25 this year, when businessman Mohammad Sharif was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town, Mohammadpur, and asked to pay Tk 10 lakh. Intelligence sources confirmed the allegations were proven during the proceedings.

Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member on October 24, who offered to help him buy a motorcycle. Four individuals later entered the flat, confined him, and demanded money, taking Tk 70,000 he had for the purchase before assaulting and threatening him.

Around 3:00 am on October 25, Sharif was reportedly forced into a car and taken out of the flat. He managed to escape near Shishu Hospital in Shyamoli after spotting a police patrol vehicle and informing them of the situation.

Police subsequently arrested six individuals, including Al Mamun and Nuruzzaman, and seized the car. The two DGFI personnel were then handed over to the army and tried under military law, resulting in their dismissal and imprisonment.
